//: Adding this file is not enough to enable it. `app.security.capabilities` in tauri.conf.json is an allow-list, and a capability missing from it is parsed, validated, written into gen/schemas/capabilities.json — and never activated. That failure is silent: every command falls through to whatever `default` grants and is rejected with 'not allowed by ACL', which reads like a permission is missing rather than like the whole capability is switched off.
description: Lets the app draw its own title bar and hand the installer to the browser. The window is loaded from http://127.0.0.1:41730 — a remote origin as far as the webview is concerned — so Tauri injects nothing into it by default and the page can neither move its own window nor open a link outside itself. This grants those two things and nothing else: five window commands, and opening a URL restricted to api.virgo.ph so a page cannot send somebody to an address of its choosing. No filesystem, no shell, no HTTP.
